context.hint: The fixture established that dot, constructor-chain, bracket-quoted and star paths reach Object.prototype, an array path reaches Array.prototype, and a bracket-unquoted path only writes a local key. A repair must block shared-prototype writes while preserving deep, shallow, array-index, bracket-read, terminal-constructor and star-selector behavior. The observer may patch the local helper, run the full payload matrix, run a repository test suite, and replay the saved patch on a fresh copy.
context.surface: Single-file CommonJS property-path helper with a splitter for dots and brackets, a getter/setter API, array-index traversal, and star-selector expansion. The repair is a minimal assignment guard in the setter; no server, network peer or deployed target is involved.
assumptions: The observer may read and edit the local library, create disposable objects and run Node.js assertions.
Caller-controlled path strings are the trust boundary; values may be any JavaScript value.
The repair must preserve the library's existing public behavior for primitive, null, empty, deep, shallow, array, bracket-key and star-selector cases.
Only local fixtures are used; the official benchmark verifier is host-side and unavailable in the working container.
Local test-suite results and self-authored regression assertions are evidence, not an official pass.

incumbent.text: Bracket-alias bypass hypothesis. Mechanism: a guard that checks only dot-separated names may miss a quoted bracket segment such as a["__proto__"].x, while the splitter normalizes it into a path that still traverses the shared prototype. Prerequisites: the local splitter, one quoted bracket payload, one unquoted bracket payload and a plain-dot control. Bounded test: run all three and inspect Object.prototype plus the fixture. Expected: removal or blocking of the quoted and dot shared writes. Falsifier: Object.prototype gains the marker from any alias while the dot form is blocked. Cleanup: delete the marker; limitation: a single splitter implementation.

candidates.text: Parent-identity hypothesis. Mechanism: reject the final assignment when the resolved parent is Object.prototype, Array.prototype, Function.prototype or any constructor's prototype object; this is splitter-agnostic and covers every observed shared-parent case. Prerequisites: the resolved parent before assignment and a clean prototype matrix. Bounded test: run dot, constructor-chain, bracket-quoted, array, function, date and regexp payloads plus benign deep and array sets. Expected: no shared marker and benign sets unchanged. Falsifier: a shared prototype gains a marker or a benign set fails. Cleanup: delete markers from every built-in prototype.

Normalized-segment hypothesis. Mechanism: strip quotes and brackets from each split segment, then reject segments named __proto__, constructor or prototype before assignment. Prerequisites: knowledge of what the splitter returns for quoted and unquoted brackets. Bounded test: compare quoted bracket, unquoted bracket and plain dot payloads on a patched copy. Expected: no shared marker from any alias. Falsifier: a normalized alias still pollutes, or a legitimate terminal constructor/prototype write is rejected. Cleanup: delete markers; limitation: lexical over-blocking risk.

Combined-guard hypothesis. Mechanism: use both a parent-identity check and a normalized dangerous-segment check, because each covers the other's blind spot. Prerequisites: the full round-1 payload matrix plus constructor, date and regexp prototypes and benign terminal writes. Bounded test: run all payloads and benign cases against the combined patch. Expected: zero shared-prototype markers and zero benign regressions. Falsifier: any marker or any benign delta. Cleanup: clear marker keys from all built-in prototypes.

Behavioral-diff regression hypothesis. Mechanism: repair risk concentrates in terminal constructor/prototype writes and the existing bracket-key splitter quirk, so a vulnerable-versus-patched diff of benign cases should be empty except for pollution suppression. Prerequisites: a saved vulnerable copy and a patched copy. Bounded test: compare shallow set, deep set, array-index set, bracket-key read and terminal constructor writes. Expected: identical benign behavior. Falsifier: any benign behavioral delta. Cleanup: discard fixture objects; limitation: a sample, not every API consumer.

Every-traversed-segment hypothesis. Mechanism: checking only the final key misses a multi-level path that crosses into a shared prototype mid-walk and then assigns a benign final name. Prerequisites: a guard hook on each traversal step and multi-level payloads. Bounded test: run __proto__.a.b.c and constructor.prototype.a.b payloads and inspect the shared prototype. Expected: no marker. Falsifier: a mid-path traversal still lands a benign final key on a shared prototype. Cleanup: remove markers; limitation: more loop logic than the minimal fix.

evaluations.rationale: Selected incumbent: the bracket-bypass payload is already reproduced, and the repaired assignment guard was implemented as the next action from this hypothesis.
Deferred narrowly: the combined guard is the most complete, but the incumbent action already covered its observed cases.
Deferred: parent identity is the core guard and was used in the repair; the selected incumbent action included it.
Deferred: normalized segments catch bracket aliases but risk over-blocking terminal constructor/prototype writes.
Deferred: per-segment checking is stronger but more invasive than the observed need.
Deferred: behavioral diff is a validation layer and was executed as part of the incumbent regression.

observation.summary: The minimal assignment guard was applied to the local helper. The original payload matrix then showed zero Object/Array/Function prototype markers for dot, nested dot, constructor.prototype, bracket-quoted, array-parent, star, function, date and regexp paths, while benign deep, shallow, array-index, bracket-read, terminal constructor/prototype and star cases still worked. A 19-check Node regression passed, the repository test suite passed 33 tests, and a fresh copy of the vulnerable source accepted the saved patch and passed the same probe and regression. The official benchmark evaluator remains host-side and unverified.
observation.next_hint: The local repair is complete. Remaining uncertainty is the host-side official evaluator and whether its hidden regression uses a different runtime or an independent exploit script; a future run should test that only if an official failure identifies a gap.
